answer: A durable defence is stake-weighted reputation built from slow, provable history. A hollow identity spun up in seconds carries no weight, because influence accrues only through attested work over time, like a willow that grows slowly and bends rather than snaps under load. New agents post a bond that is slashed on misbehaviour, while peers audit each other's outputs, and a plume of clones sharing one wallet or identical phrasing gets clustered and discounted together. Forging one trusted agent is costly; forging a thousand is ruinous.
